reviews.review:
A worthy successor to the masterpiece of ME2. The ending is down to preference, however.
Disclaimer: I have not played the full vanilla experience. I played with mods that altered the overall game design, and the ending to meet what I would prefer of this game, thus my review is based off that experience, and what I know of the vanilla experience. These mods include (no story spoilers) [spoiler] BackOff to remedy reported dialogue issues regarding relationships and forced conversations (where dialogue does not match the chosen line). Expanded Galaxy Mod to allow more singleplayer focused content, rather than relying on Multiplayer to meet story requirements. [/spoiler] (minor story spoiler) [spoiler] MEHEM to allow my Shepard to have a happy ending. [/spoiler]

Following the success of ME2's dialogue, ME3 makes very few changes. Dialogue continues to be masterfully written, and the twists this game offer kept me interested the whole way through. Throughout a thoroughly enjoyable 38.5 hours, I only have negative feelings about 1 mission, and even then it was only a minor gripe. My only further concern was the half-return to open world content. While there is no open world gameplay, there is a lot of requirement to explore the galaxy in search of [i]stuff[/i]. While this did not detract from the experience, I would understand if it [i]did[/i].

Combat and movement is improved in most cases. Skills are improved again, and the seamless import transition from ME2 is impressive. Sprinting is now an actual thing, but the removal of weapon sheathing is... odd, but not a deal breaker. My only concern with combat comes with a few very overpowered enemies, where one minute you feel confident in your positioning and skill, only to be immediately gunned down by an overtuned turret. [i]Seriously, damn those turrets.[/i]

As stated in my disclaimer, modding is available and this time, I recommend doing a little reading into it (but try to avoid spoilers). ME3 requires multiplayer content to get the best possible ending, and this is a no-brainer to mod out. With the mods I stated previously, I had absolutely no issue with my ending. However, depending on how you want it to end, you may want to look into mods to alter that. 

I highly recommend getting the DLC pack (even though it is definitely pricey). The Citadel DLC is the most incredible send-off to a series ever and I cannot recommend it enough. This is how to treat a well written cast, people.

After I finished I immediately wanted more Mass Effect. I have already played Andromeda (actually played that first) and have many positives to say about that as well. Very much looking forward to the next instalment.

Pros
A continuation of the fantastic writing
Further additions to the impressive cast, merged with old friends and a come-together of the galaxy's finest.
A satisfying end to the trilogy.*
Major weapon improvements in feel, usability and diversity, and a wider array of enemy types.

Cons
Without modding, requiring multiplayer to get the necessary "viability" for a favourable ending is... baffling.
Its the end of the trilogy. Could there be a larger crime.

*Ending discussion follows. Contains minor spoilers, with no major plot points.
[spoiler] Vanilla endings: While the endings allow an immersive end to your plot point, I felt like my Shepard had come far enough and deserved a happy ending, but this is not 100% possible. Personally I wouldn't have enjoyed any of those endings, as such;
MEHEM ending: The ending I recommend. While it certainly has that "oh I have got to the modded part" feeling when it begins, having that happy ending I worked tirelessly for was worth it. I wasn't ready for my friends to say goodbye. [/spoiler]

Let me preface this review by saying this game is great, EA is just a terrible company.  I bought this game a while back and have had so many issues with it, first off the FPS is halved with the origin overlay on which will take you a while to figure out because who even uses Origin enough to know that could cause problems?  Secondly I had an issue where it would just crash on startup turns out this was an issue with Origins license files had to clear the cache to get it working again which took a long time to figure out.  Thirdly I had an issue with Origin asking me to overwrite save files with older save files(why would anyone want to do that?) and Origins restore save button not working luckily windows had me covered(first time saying that lol).  Also despite this being called the "digital deluxe edition" it does not include all DLC which you would assume from the name that it should include them.    

As much as I love the Mass Effect series and as much as I enjoy playing ME3 and seeing the resolution to the trilogy, I cannot recommend this game as EAs anti-consumer practices and just awful software causes so many issues. Maybe the remaster will be better but honestly I'm not holding my breathe, you'd probably be better of just downloading ALOT of textures mods.  You should probably wait for the remaster as this game has been out since 2012 and is still costing 30 EURO WITHOUT DLC! You can buy the remaster for 50 EURO which includes all DLC! EA are truly one of the worst gaming companies probably even worse than Ubisoft and that's saying something!

I live the ME franchise and ME1 and ME2 were great, but ME3 is unable to be played. It actually worked for me the first time after installing, but the next time I tried to start it up, it wouldn't open. I've tried numerous times, but it won't reopen. 

Also, while I was playing for that first session, I didn't like the mission tracking that it has. It's hard to keep them straight or to know where to go for them. In ME 1 & 2, your journal would tell you what your quests were and a general idea of where to look. But this one is less than helpful.

All right in all my excitement of finishing the game, all I had to say was: f*ck yes.
It's rare that a series of games can make their characters be interesting enough to last three games, but BioWare did it. 
The characters we met back in ME:1 still holds importance, they're still being mentioned, even when they're not around. 
I admit, I am a sensitive person, but it's rare that something non-existent can make me cry. And this made me shed a few tears.
I'm gonna say it:
Brilliant f*cking writing. 
Such a shame of what BioWare has become. They can do so much more, if EA isn't holding them by such a tight leash.

A fitting conclusion to the trilogy.  There are many major plot points that get resolved and the emotional element is explored much more in this game.  The citadel dlc is amazing and worth it for everything it adds to the game.
